Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.web.security

Class SpringSecurityConfig

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.web.security.SpringSecurityConfig
@Configuration @EnableMethodSecurity public class SpringSecurityConfig extends Object
Spring Security configuration for the JWT and API-key authenticated chain (design §8.1).

Filter order, outermost to innermost:

  1. RateLimitFilter — global Bucket4j gate. Unauthenticated traffic counts too (REQ-RL-003). Skips /actuator/** via shouldNotFilter.
  2. JwtAuthenticationFilter — populates UserPrincipal when Authorization: Bearer ... is valid.
  3. ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter — populates SystemPrincipal when X-Client-Id + X-Api-Key validate AND no JWT-driven authentication is already on the context. "JWT wins" per design §8.1.
  4. ForcedPasswordChangeFilter — blocks most endpoints when the current user has mustChangePassword=true; transparent to SystemPrincipal.

/api/v1/admin/** requires ROLE_ADMIN at the URL layer (design §8.6); STANDARD JWTs and SYSTEM API-key callers are both 403 there. The class-level @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") on ApiKeysAdminController is defense in depth on top of this rule, which is why EnableMethodSecurity is on.
